messages.author: a0bb4bbabc692a8e
messages.subject: Importing Files
parts:
I am new to using R and I am trying to import files for methylKit analysis. I am having trouble importing methylation call files from Bismark output. I keep getting an error message "Error in `[.data.frame`(data, , 6) : undefined columns selected" 

I have 6 files:

CpG_context_B73_anther.txt
CpG_context_B73_meiocyte.txt
CpG_context_B73_seedling.txt
CpG_context_CML228_anther.txt
CpG_context_CML228_meiocyte.txt
CpG_context_CML228_seedling.txt

The syntax I used is below:

file.list = list("CpG_context_B73_anther.txt", "CpG_context_B73_meiocyte.txt",
"CpG_context_B73_seedling.txt", "CpG_context_CML228_anther.txt", "CpG_context_CML_meiocyte.txt", "CpG_context_CML_seedling.txt")

methRead(file.list, sample.id = list("B73anther", "B73meiocyte", "B73seedling", "CML228anther", "CML228meiocyte", "CML228seedling"), assembly = "B73_V3", pipeline = "bismark", treatment = c(0,0,0,1,1,1), context = "CpG")

I patterned the syntax based on the documentation. Is there something wrong with it?

Thank you very much,

Nelson

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Importing Files
parts:
Please send a reproducible example. It is likely you are using the wrong file format. There are plenty of examples in the docs what legitimate file would look like

Best
Altuna

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Importing Files
parts:
Hi Altuna, 

I also think it is a wrong file format. Alternatively, I tried "processBismarkAln" on the bam files and it worked! My objective is to visualize (make a graph of) methylation across chromosomes using my samples. I tiled them first using "tileMethylCounts" and then called "percMethylation" and I got the the following:

> head (percMethylationTiled)
  CML_anther_CpG_chr01 CML_meiocyte_CpG_chr01 CML_seedling_CpG_chr01.txt
1             90.00000              100.00000                  100.00000
2            100.00000              100.00000                   90.90909
3             80.00000              100.00000                  100.00000
4             84.09091               95.83333                  100.00000
5             97.29730               96.11650                   97.79412
6             83.82979               91.91919                   55.00000

However, as you can see, the information about the chromosome coordinates is gone, so I cannot plot the percent methylation against the chromosome coordinates anymore. 

Is there a way to preserve the chromosome coordinate information when using "percMethylation"?

Regards,
Nelson

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Importing Files
parts:
percMethylation has arguments to keep the coordinates as row names. However, the order of the data doesn't change when you call percMethylation() on a methylBase object. You can take the coordinates from the methylBase object.

Best,
Altuna
